title: Deployment decision canvas + facilitator notes for customer POC
summary: Working facilitator guide and slide outline to run a 3-hour customer workshop focused on finalizing model selection, routing/fallback policies, and acceptance criteria for a production POC. Emphasis on decisions that unblock engineering and SRE work for Dedicated or Private deployment.
agenda:
1) 0:00 - 0:15 Introductions & objectives: quick round, confirm outcomes
2) 0:15 - 0:40 Current state walkthrough (customer leads): data volume, latency needs, privacy constraints
3) 0:40 - 1:10 Model capabilities and tradeoffs: open models vs. quantized variants (team demo)
4) 1:10 - 1:30 Decision canvas activity: constraints, SLOs, cost targets (breakout)
5) 1:30 - 1:50 Break & capture parking lot
6) 1:50 - 2:30 Routing and fallback design: region routing, dedicated vs hosted, canary plan
7) 2:30 - 2:50 Acceptance criteria & metrics: test prompts, regressions, latency windows
8) 2:50 - 3:00 Next steps and action owners
slide_outline:
Slide 1: Workshop goals and success measures
Slide 2: Current architecture snapshot (customer-provided) - ask for missing pieces
Slide 3: Workload profile summary (QPS, token distribution, peak patterns)
Slide 4: Candidate models and perf summary (accuracy proxies, latency, cost/unit)
Slide 5: Decision canvas template - constraints, SLOs, risk tolerance, preferred topology
Slide 6: Routing strategy options with visuals (single-region, multi-region, hybrid)
Slide 7: Fallback & graceful degradation patterns (model downgraded variant, cached responses)
Slide 8: Canary testing plan - traffic percentages, duration, rollback triggers
Slide 9: Acceptance test rubric (exact-match, semantic similarity thresholds, latency p95)
Slide 10: Implementation checklist and owners
Slide 11: Parking lot and unanswered questions
Slide 12: Next steps and agreed milestones
facilitation_notes: Start by validating objectives aloud. Use a 2-minute lightning round so everyone states one success metric. For the decision canvas activity: split into two breakout groups - product+customer-success in one, eng+SRE in the other. Give 12 minutes, then 6 minutes reporting back. Watch for micro-concerns around data residency - if raised, surface private deployment options and call out additional compliance tasks. For routing discussion: provide concrete examples (route 80% to dedicated pool, 20% to hosted fallback). Emphasize measurable rollback triggers: p95 latency > target by 20% for 5m, or error rate > 2% sustained 10m. Encourage writing acceptance prompts now; capture 6 canonical prompts that exercise edge-cases. Keep tempo: if debates run long, park details and decide owners to draft configs post-workshop. Note to facilitator: have access to cost calculator sheet, model perf table, and a whiteboard link. Keep end-time strict and assign action owners in the last 5 minutes.
materials_and_prep: Pre-reads to send 48h before: 1) workload profile template (sheet), 2) short model perf matrix, 3) proposed decision canvas PDF. Bring laptop for live demo of 1 model variant. SRE should pre-populate current infra diagram. Bring the cost calc export (csv) and latest p99/p95 latency from observability console. Ask customer to identify 2 subject-matter SMEs and 1 network contact for private/VPC questions.
success_criteria:
- Agreement on 1 primary model variant for initial POC and 1 fallback variant
- Written acceptance test set (min 6 prompts) committed to the POC repo
- Owner assigned for routing policy, canary plan, and rollback triggers
- Draft deployment timeline with milestone dates (canary start, full rollout)
- Identified compliance blockers for Private deployment (if any)
open_questions:
- Does the customer require FIPS or specific KMS integration for the POC?
- What is the realistic monthly token budget they are willing to commit to for Dedicated capacity?
- Are there external latency constraints from downstream systems (e.g., synchronous user flows)?
- Is dataset for acceptance tests available and scrubbed for PII?
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Model quality regression after quantization. Mitigation: Hold a short eval sweep comparing full fp16 vs quantized on 300-case prompt set; require no more than X% drop in semantic similarity.
Risk: Network egress constraints for Private deployments. Mitigation: Engage infra/network early and provision VPC endpoints; allow hosted fallback for initial tests.
Risk: Cost overrun during canary. Mitigation: Cap traffic and use token budget alerts; scheduled automatic rollback if budget threshold hit.
next_steps:
1) Within 48h: facilitator to post workshop notes and raw decision canvases to Confluence and tag owners
2) Within 5 business days: engineering to produce deployment config draft for canary
3) Customer: share acceptance prompt set and scrubbed sample data
4) Schedule 30-min follow-up to finalize timeline and sign-off
notes_to_self: Keep phrasing neutral when discussing model failures; avoid promising SLA-level latency during POC. If customer asks for benchmarks vs competitor X, offer to run a focused microbenchmark after the POC scope is agreed. Capture any specific phrasing the customer wants surfaced in user-facing docs.
